title: RecoveryRecordV1
description:
A human backup of a transport identity: the 24 words plus the non-secret metadata needed to verify a restore.

THIS SHAPE IS A BEARER SECRET. Anyone holding `words` can reconstruct the private key and impersonate that PeerId until peers revoke trust. It never crosses IPC, MCP, Claude Channel, the transport network, the endpoint directory, discovery, or Kademlia — export and restore are offline local operations only (ADR-0033). A schema for it exists so a backup file can be validated offline, NOT because the record is ever transmitted.

`expected_peer_id` is public metadata and is load-bearing: the BIP-39 checksum for 256-bit entropy is only 8 bits, so the PeerId is what actually proves a restore reconstructed the intended identity. A checksum-valid phrase deriving a different PeerId is a hard failure with no 'close enough' fallback.

format.description: Uses ONLY BIP-39's entropy-to-mnemonic encoding. The wallet derivation PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512(mnemonic, "mnemonic"+passphrase, 2048) is explicitly not used, and there is no recovery passphrase — the 256-bit entropy IS the Ed25519 secret seed. Feeding these words into a cryptocurrency wallet produces unrelated material.

identity_algorithm.description: Restore must refuse any other algorithm rather than attempt a conversion.

expected_peer_id.description: Optional in the record only because a phrase may survive alone. When present, restore requires an exact match.

items.description: English BIP-39 wordlist only. The list is ASCII, though input is NFKD-normalized before lookup.

words.description: EXACTLY 24 words — 256 bits of entropy plus an 8-bit checksum. The 12/15/18/21-word BIP-39 lengths are rejected for this format rather than accepted with less entropy, so the schema pins the count at both ends.
